summary.intent: Wrap up PR #37 (parallel batch upload pipeline) by addressing code review threads, then update all planning and documentation on a docs branch — including DEFERRED.md, FEATURES.md, README.md, and a new filesystem specification.
summary.outcome: PR #37 was merged to main after fixing 3 of 4 review threads (postMessage try/catch, doc comment) and deferring 1 (lazy file reading). On a docs branch, DEFERRED.md, FEATURES.md, and README.md were updated, and a new FILESYSTEM_SPECIFICATION.md was created and committed.

repo: Batch upload is implemented in the JS/TS SDK but NOT in the Rust SDK — feature matrix must reflect this gap.
Lazy file reading within the concurrency pool (useDropUpload.ts:140) requires an SDK contract change to accept File objects or a read callback instead of Uint8Array — deferred as architectural work.
The CipherBox filesystem must conform to Windows-style case-insensitive naming as the strictest common denominator across Desktop OSes.
Phase planning docs live under .planning/phases/<phase-slug>/ with PLAN, SUMMARY, CONTEXT, DISCUSSION-LOG, RESEARCH, VALIDATION, and VERIFICATION files.
Preliminary R&D docs were renamed/moved into .planning/milestones/m0/ during the main merge.

code.finding: File reads happen eagerly inside the concurrency pool; lazy reading requires SDK API change to accept File objects instead of Uint8Array.
encrypt() needed try/catch around getWorker()/postMessage() — both CodeRabbit and Copilot independently flagged the same missing error boundary.

workflow: When multiple reviewers (CodeRabbit + Copilot) flag the same issue independently, it is a strong signal the fix is necessary but also that future review rounds yield diminishing returns.
Deferred items should be cross-referenced between PR review threads and the central DEFERRED.md to avoid re-litigating the same architectural decisions in every review cycle.
Parallel agent research (phases, feature state, filesystem rules) significantly accelerates large documentation update tasks.

friction: Copilot's batch memory thread (#3) was a duplicate of an already-tracked CodeRabbit deferred item — reviewers had no visibility into existing deferred decisions, causing redundant discussion.
E2E test coverage and feature matrix in FEATURES.md were stale enough to require a dedicated update pass after every major feature merge.
